portName: Port of Stavanger (Vågen: Strandkaien and Skagenkaien)
seoTitle: Stavanger cruise port guide: Vågen, Lysefjord, Pulpit Rock
seoDescription: Stavanger cruise ships berth in Vågen, 500 m from the centre. Pulpit Rock: 8 km, about 4 hours on foot plus 1 hour by bus each way. Cathedral NOK 75 (2026).
quickAnswer: Ships normally berth at Strandkaien or Skagenkaien in Vågen, the inner harbour, about 500 m from the city centre, so you walk off the ship into town. Old Stavanger, the cathedral and the Petroleum Museum are all on foot. For Pulpit Rock, be on a return bus that reaches Stavanger at least 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Stavanger is a dock-in-town port. The cruise quays line Vågen, the old harbour, with Old Stavanger's white wooden houses rising on one side and the cathedral a few minutes away. The town itself fills a half day easily on foot. The big decision is whether to go out to the Lysefjord: either a 3–3.5 hour fjord cruise from the same harbour, or the Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) hike, which uses most of a normal call and leaves little margin if anything runs late.
tenderNotes: Ships normally berth. Anchorage in the Åmøyfjord with tendering is possible, and on busy days a ship may be given a berth outside the centre, in which case shuttle buses are often provided; check your ship's daily programme.

terminals.name: Strandkaien (Vågen, west side)
terminals.notes: Main cruise quay, 309 m. Below Old Stavanger. No dedicated terminal building; you step off onto the harbour front.

terminals.name: Skagenkaien (Vågen, east side)
terminals.notes: 149 m quay on the east side of the harbour, by the tourist office and the old sea houses.

terminals.name: Skansekaien and Konserthuskaien
terminals.notes: Further quays at the harbour mouth used when several ships call. The port lists berths as 100–800 m from the tourist information.

walkability.detail: From the Vågen quays the centre, Old Stavanger and the cathedral are a short, mostly level walk. Old Stavanger's lanes are cobbled and slope up from the harbour. If your ship is sent to a berth outside the centre, use the shuttle.

transportSections.detail: Old Stavanger is directly above Strandkaien. The cathedral is a few minutes inland from the head of the harbour. The Lysefjord boats leave from Strandkaien, 10–15 minutes from the moorings.

transportSections.cost: NOK 49 one zone, NOK 87 two zones; NOK 20 extra if bought on board (2026)
transportSections.time: Ticket valid 60 min in one zone
transportSections.detail: Buy in the Kolumbus Billett app, Entur app or at ticket machines before boarding. You do not need a bus for the centre.

transportSections.cost: Book online in advance; tickets are not sold on the bus
transportSections.time: About 1 hour each way to Preikestolen BaseCamp
transportSections.detail: Seasonal, April to September. Departs from Olav Vs gate 3, by the Radisson Blu Atlantic Hotel, about 500 m from Strandkaien/Skagenkaien. Return tickets are generally not valid on another company's bus.

transportSections.cost: Listed at NOK 890 on the operator's site (2026)
transportSections.detail: Rødne's Lysefjord cruise leaves from Strandkaien in Vågen and passes below Preikestolen. Be at the boat 20 minutes before departure; seats are not allocated.

returnTiming.rule: From the centre, start back 70 minutes before all-aboard. From Preikestolen, take a return bus that reaches Stavanger at least 90 minutes before all-aboard: for a 17:30 all-aboard, that is the 15:00 bus from the trailhead.
returnTiming.detail: The hike is about 8 km return with around 500 m of climbing and needs about four hours; with an hour's bus each way, the trip takes roughly six hours. There is one road route and seasonal buses at fixed times, so a slow walker or a missed bus has no quick fix. The Lysefjord boat returns to Strandkaien, a 10–15 minute walk from the ship.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you miss your return bus from Preikestolen, call the bus operator straight away and then the port agent number on your ship's daily programme. A taxi is the only other fast option back to Stavanger, and it is expensive.

excursionAdvice: Skip the ship's tour for Stavanger itself: everything central is a short walk. The independent Lysefjord boat leaves from the same harbour and is easy to do alone. Preikestolen is the case for the ship's tour: it takes about six hours door to door, buses sell out in summer, and the ship will wait for its own tour if the bus or the weather causes delays. Book independently only if your call is at least nine hours and you are a confident hiker.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 at Strandkaien and all-aboard is 17:30, in summer.

steps.what: Walk up from the quay into Old Stavanger and wander the lanes of white wooden houses.
Walk round the head of the harbour to Stavanger Cathedral (NOK 75).
Øvre Holmegate, the colour street, then the Vågen harbour front and the tourist office at Skagenkaien.
Norwegian Petroleum Museum (NOK 180; open 10:00–19:00 in summer).
Lunch by the harbour, for example seafood at Fisketorget.
Option: climb to Valberg Tower for the view over Vågen, or rest on the harbour front. On a long call, take the Lysefjord boat instead of the museum.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Old Stavanger (Gamle Stavanger)
sights.why: More than 170 preserved white wooden houses on cobbled lanes just above the cruise quay.
sights.tip: Go first, before the lanes fill with tour groups.

sights.name: Stavanger Cathedral
sights.why: Begun around 1125, the only medieval cathedral in Norway that has kept its original architecture; restored 2015–2024.
sights.tip: It closes to visitors during services and events; check the day's hours.

sights.name: Norwegian Petroleum Museum
sights.why: How oil and gas shaped modern Norway, on the harbour front.
sights.tip: Open daily 10:00–19:00 from June to August; shorter hours the rest of the year.

sights.name: Øvre Holmegate (Fargegaten)
sights.why: A short street of brightly painted facades with cafés and small shops.
sights.tip: Combine with the harbour front on the east side of Vågen.

sights.name: Vågen harbour front
sights.why: The old sea houses along Strandkaien and Skagenkaien, now restaurants and bars.
sights.tip: The tourist office is on Skagenkaien.

sights.name: Valberg Tower (Valbergtårnet)
sights.why: A former watchtower above the east side of Vågen with a view over the harbour.
sights.tip: A short, steep climb from the harbour.

sights.name: Lysefjord cruise
sights.why: Sails up the Lysefjord and below Preikestolen, 604 m above the water.
sights.tip: Leaves from Strandkaien; be there 20 minutes early.

sights.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
sights.why: The flat-topped cliff 604 m above the Lysefjord.
sights.tip: About 8 km return and 500 m of climbing on rock, stairs and boardwalk. Wear walking shoes and carry rain gear and water.

beaches.name: Solastranden
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi, or Kolumbus bus (plan the route in the Kolumbus app)
beaches.time: Near Stavanger Airport, about 14 km from the port
beaches.note: Long sandy beach. Too far for a short call; the water is cold even in summer.

Restaurants around Vågen; ask whether it is made in-house

food.dish: Skillingsboller (cinnamon buns) or waffles with brunost
food.where: Bakeries and cafés in the centre

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning Preikestolen on a short call.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow about six hours. Only go on a call of nine hours or more, or take the ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up for the Preikestolen bus without a ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Book online in advance; tickets are not sold on the bus and summer departures sell out.

commonMistakes.mistake: Hiking in town shoes and no rain layer.
commonMistakes.fix: The trail is rock, stairs and boggy ground, and plateau weather differs from the harbour. Wear walking shoes and carry a waterproof.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying a bus ticket on board.
commonMistakes.fix: It costs NOK 20 extra. Use the Kolumbus app, or simply walk: the centre needs no bus.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming your ship berths in Vågen.
commonMistakes.fix: On busy days ships can be placed further out. Check the daily programme for the berth and any shuttle.

safety: Stavanger is a safe city for visitors. The main risks are outdoors: the Preikestolen plateau has unfenced cliff edges and the trail can be slippery when wet. Keep well back from the edge and turn round if the weather closes in. In town, Old Stavanger's cobbles are slippery in rain.
accessibility: The Vågen quays and harbour front are level, and the cathedral and Petroleum Museum are a short, flat walk. Old Stavanger is cobbled and slopes up from the harbour, so it is hard going for wheelchairs. Preikestolen is unsuitable for wheelchairs despite trail improvements. The Lysefjord boat is the step-light way to see the fjord; ask the operator about access before booking.
rainyDay: Rain is common. Spend longer in the Norwegian Petroleum Museum and the cathedral, then eat by the harbour. The Lysefjord boat still runs in rain, but the view may be lost in low cloud. Skip Preikestolen in heavy rain or fog: the rock is slippery and the view will be gone.
crowdTips: Several ships can call on the same day. Old Stavanger and the harbour front are busiest mid-morning, when groups come off the ships. Go up into Old Stavanger first, visit the museum around midday, and book Preikestolen buses and Lysefjord boats early in high season.

faqs.q: Is Stavanger walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships berth in Vågen, about 500 m from the centre. Old Stavanger is right above the quay.
Normally no; ships berth at Strandkaien or Skagenkaien. Tendering is possible but uncommon, and on busy days a ship may berth further out with a shuttle.

faqs.q: Can I hike Pulpit Rock from a cruise ship in Stavanger?
faqs.a: Only on a long call. The bus takes about an hour each way and the hike about four hours. Be on a return bus that reaches Stavanger at least 90 minutes before all-aboard.

faqs.q: How long is the Lysefjord cruise from Stavanger?
faqs.a: 3–3.5 hours, leaving from Strandkaien in Vågen, a 10–15 minute walk from the cruise moorings.

faqs.q: What can I do in Stavanger in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Old Stavanger, the cathedral, Øvre Holmegate and the Petroleum Museum on foot, or a Lysefjord boat trip.

faqs.q: How much does Stavanger Cathedral cost?
Do I need a bus in Stavanger?
faqs.a: Not for the centre. A Kolumbus single ticket costs NOK 49 for one zone (2026), bought in the app.
Yes. Take care on the Preikestolen cliffs and on wet cobbles.
